```{r, setup, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(magrittr)
library(driveanalytics)

knitr::opts_knit$set(echo = FALSE)

# Get the render format
render_format <- knitr::opts_knit$get('rmarkdown.pandoc.to')
if (render_format == "") render_format <- "html"
```


## Background
This analysis computes the relative risk and odds ratios for events between cohorts.
It can be used to identify which events are more likely to occur in a specific cohort, relative to another.
The methods produces an ordered plot and tabulated data with the relative risk/odds ratio values and 95% confidence intervals for a given cohort relative to the selected 'relative' cohort.

## Method
The relative risk values for any event within the cohort is calculated using the BMJ method [1].
In the case than an event does not occur in a cohort, 0.5 events are added to all cohorts.

## Considerations and Limitations
* Risk ratios are raw risks of event occurrence. No confounding factors are identified or considered.
* The method does not account for multiple comparisons.

## Example
The following plot and table show the relative risk for a weighted-random set of events in 100 subjects.

This example shows the following information:

1. The relative risk for events A and B are significantly higher in cohort B than in cohort A (i.e., the relative risk and 95% confidence interval values are above 100%).
1. The majority of the events are not significantly more prevelent in either cohort.
1. The relative risk for events C and G are significantly lower in cohort B than in cohort A.

```{r, example, echo=FALSE, dpi=200, out.width="100%", fig.dim = c(8, 3)}

# Create a random sample of patients in two cohorts and assign random events
set.seed(123)
n <- 100
nev <- n * 5
df_pde <- tibble::tibble(
  project_id = 1:n,
  cohort_id = project_id,
  cohort = sample(c("A","B"), n, replace = TRUE),
)
df_dia <- df_pde %>%
  dplyr::sample_n(nev, replace = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(event = sample(paste0("Event ", LETTERS[1:10]), nev, replace = TRUE)) %>%
  # Make event A more common in cohort B
  dplyr::mutate(event = dplyr::if_else(cohort == "B" & runif(nev) > 0.7, "Event A", event)) %>%
  # Make event B more common in cohort B
  dplyr::mutate(event = dplyr::if_else(cohort == "B" & runif(nev) > 0.7, "Event B", event))

# Perform analysis and get results
gfa <- driveanalytics::gen_frequency_analysis(df_dia, df_pde, "event", "cohort")
gca <- driveanalytics::gen_correlation_analysis(gfa, "A")
gca_head <- head(gca, 26)
plot(gca_head)
tabulate(gca_head, render_format)

```

## References
[1] BMJ description of method for calculating event risk


[1]: https://bestpractice.bmj.com/info/toolkit/learn-ebm/how-to-calculate-risk/
